features.headline: Would any USMNT players really make Man United better if they followed Poch?
features.desc: Now that USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino has taken over Man United, would it make sense for USMNT players to join their ex-coach?
body: If you follow the U.S. men's national team, here's a good sanity check: Imagine going back in time — say, 15 years — and telling your past self about the current situation.

"Yeah, so there's this guy who came up through the FC Dallas academy, moved to Schalke when he was a kid, started for them as an 18-year-old when they finished second in the Bundesliga behind Bayern Munich, and then moved to Juventus.
He has played more Serie A matches for Juve than anyone else in the seven seasons since he joined the team."

"And he just did this news conference where he said, 'Guys from here being talked about going to Manchester United' was 'inevitable.' Oh, and this is important: he was saying that because Manchester United just poached the USMNT manager in the middle of the Premier League season."

Think about all the assumptions your 15-years-younger self would be making, whenever they had regained consciousness after suffering the double-whammy of learning that time travel exists and that the USMNT was one step below Manchester United in the global pecking order.
... Schalke are one of the best development clubs in the world, and Juventus are one of the best clubs in the world, so one of the best soccer players in the world plays for the USMNT now?

And then, well, the USMNT coach is now coaching Manchester United, which might be the best club in the world. If my math is right, then there was a World Cup a couple of months ago — in summer 2026 — so... wait... did the U.S. just win the World Cup?

features.headline: Bills edge Chiefs with last-second FG in low-scoring battle
features.desc: The Bills won their seventh straight, snapping the Chiefs' win streak at three in a sloppy, low-scoring thriller.
body: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — Special teams were the difference in the Buffalo Bills' last-second Thanksgiving night win over the Kansas City Chiefs. Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired at Highmark Stadium to give the Bills a signature 13-10 win over the Chiefs.

The field goal was set up by a tipped punt and ensuing Greg Dortch return to set up the Bills in field goal range where, despite the wet and wintry conditions, Bass connected a low kick through the uprights to finish off the low-scoring affair.

The Bills (10-1) came into Thursday's action not having allowed a touchdown in 15 quarters, and then, aided by the weather, managed to keep Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs (8-3) out of the end zone until the third quarter.
For as impressive as this Kansas City rushing attack has looked in recent weeks, the Bills mostly kept it in check.

And the Bills' pass rush forced Mahomes out of his comfort zone pretty regularly, but as Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard pointed out early in the week, Mahomes has a knack for winning reps even when the defense does everything right.
The same can usually be said about Allen, but that just wasn't the case in this one.

With temperatures in the low 30s, Allen's passer rating was seldom even half of that. He extended a few drives with his legs and benefitted from a game plan that revolved more around James Cook III runs than the passing attack.
Still, the Bills' superpower this season has been pairing long drives with one of the league's best red zone offenses.

features.headline: Joe Milton has huge game as Eagles shock Cowboys
features.desc: Dallas blew a 21-point lead as Philly made a spectacular comeback with Milton at the helm.
body: ARLINGTON, Texas — Quarterback Joe Milton shined on the national stage, helping erase a 21-point third-quarter deficit to lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a thrilling 39-38 shootout win over the Dallas Cowboys to keep some hope alive in what's been a trying season.

Milton accounted for four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) and made a number of "wow" throws with his howitzer arm, the bulk of which went to receiver DeVonta Smith, who erupted for 186 receiving yards and two scores.
Milton did enough in the closing moments to set up a game-winning 59-yard field goal by Jake Elliott.

Any progress the defense made following quality outings against the New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers in consecutive games was stopped cold by a Dallas attack that was a clear step up in weight class, but the Eagles firmed up late to give Philly a chance.

Injuries hit, as they have all season, with running back Saquon Barkley (stinger), defensive back Cooper DeJean (concussion), tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder), safety Marcus Epps (foot) and defensive tackle Gabe Hall (wrist) all forced to the sideline.

But with a pair of gettable games coming up against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, it's not inconceivable the Eagles could turn this into a four-game winning streak as they attempt to climb out of the NFC East basement.
Here are the most important things to know from Thursday night for both teams:

What to make of the QB performance: The Eagles have something with Milton. He's shown playmaking ability in three starts since being signed off the Cowboys' practice squad last month, including a pair of long touchdown passes to Smith on Thursday.

features.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
features.desc: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
body: Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.
In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game.
Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.
On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks.
It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.
Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.
Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

It's been three seasons of injuries and subpar results since Luis Robert Jr. had his big year in 2023 for the Chicago White Sox, when he hit.264 with 38 home runs, 75 extra-base hits and plus defense in center field.

Yet we still dream the magic will somehow return, even as he now enters his age-29 season. The Baltimore Orioles are certainly dreaming big, believing Robert can be their full-time center fielder in 2027.
The best guess here: It's unlikely to happen. There's nothing from the past three seasons that suggests Robert can stay healthy and also hit the way he did in 2023.
Over the past three seasons, averaging 90 games per season, he has hit.223/.290/.379 for a subpar OPS+ of 88.
That includes three games in 2026 with the Orioles, who claimed him off waivers from the Mets in August — only to see Robert immediately go down with a hamstring injury.

That didn't scare them off. Look, Robert is enticing. He still has power and is still capable of playing at least a decent center field — two attributes the Orioles didn't get from their center fielders in 2026.
